summary_paragraph: A 68-year-old woman was admitted with acute chest pain radiating to the jaw and shoulder, diagnosed as NSTEMI based on elevated troponin and EKG changes. She underwent cardiac catheterization, which revealed severe three-vessel disease. The LAD artery was dilated with balloon angioplasty, but no stent was placed due to her underlying immune thrombocytopenic purpura and platelet count of 80,000. The RCA was chronically occluded and left untreated, and the circumflex could not be engaged due to tortuosity. She was pre-treated for contrast allergy and tolerated the procedure well. Her isosorbide mononitrate was increased to 60 mg daily, and she was started on a one-month course of clopidogrel. She remained stable, with troponin trending down, and was discharged home in good condition with cardiology follow-up planned.
problems: Atherosclerotic heart disease of native coronary artery without angina pectoris
Personal history of malignant neoplasm of breast
